## Question 145 (Year: 2014 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

**Question ID: 2014-gs3-q145-unacademy**
**Q13. Should the pursuit of carbon credits and clean development mechanisms set up under UNFCCC be maintained even though there has been a massive slide in the value of a carbon credit? Discuss with respect to India’s energy needs for economic growth. (250 Words, 15 Marks). Tag: Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment.**

#

## Answer

## **Decoding the Question**

- **In intro try to define carbon credits and** **also in brief write about clean development** **mechanism.**-**In Body,**-**Discuss reasons for reduced value of** **carbon credits.**-**In the second part, justify whether India** **should pursue for carbon credits or fulfil** **domestic energy demand. (Balanced** **answer needed, write need of energy for** **India, and also need of carbon credits)**-**Try to conclude the answer with a balanced** **opinion.** **Answer:** A carbon credit is a permit that allows the company that holds it to emit a certain amount of carbon dioxide or other greenhouse gases. One credit permits the emission of a mass equal to one ton of carbon dioxide. The Clean Development Mechanism (CDM9 established under the UN’s Kyoto Protocol has two main goals: First, to assist countries without emissions targets (i.e. developing countries) in achieving sustainable development and Second, help those countries with emission reduction targets under Kyoto (i.e. developed countries) in achieving compliance by allowing them to purchase offsets created by CDM projects. Carbon credit trading, once seen as one of the most successful mechanisms to help developed countries and the private sector to continue with business while meeting their emission targets, is now on the brink of disappearing into oblivion.

## **Reasons for decline in value of carbon credits**

- **FallendemandintheEuropeanmarket:Therehas** been decreasing demand in European countries for carbon credit which leads to a massive price decrease of carbon credit.
- **Domestic market:** Countries like Canada, China, Brazil, have set up independent carbon markets they can trade in, without the prices being influenced by global circumstances. This led to a fall in prices of global carbon credit.
- **Restrictions of purchase:** European countries and countries like Australia have put restrictions and put a cap on purchase of carbon credits from developing countries like India.
- **No commitment under Kyoto Protocol:** The talks to extend the commitment made under Kyoto Protocol have not materialised into any agreement. This has hurt business sentiments and dissuaded businesses from opting for a clean energy mechanism. India, the second largest populated nation in the world with more than a billion people has an economy which is growing at nearly 8% over the last decade and about 6% on the average since her independence in 1947. India’s economy is already very energy hungry and demand is set grow enormously.

## **Should India pursue for carbon credits and CDM**

- **Demand of Energy:** Due to increasing demand for energy, India has put a lot of emphasis on improving energy efficiency. The continued pursuit for carbon credit will be very negative for India’s energy sector and this can compromise India’s energy needs.
- **ManufacturingHub:India’squestforcarboncredits** can be harmful to make India a manufacturing hub and improve quality of life. As carbon credit may prove detrimental for growth in the energy sector and even harms newer investments.
- **Huge Population:** India can not depend on clean energy completely for fulfilling its energy needs. As India have huge population and going to become number one in terms of population size and to achieve Sustainable Development Goals Indian ned huge investments in energy sector.
- **Use for Own Benefit:** Indian need to use surplus carbon credit for its own benefits by selling it domestically. It will achieve twin objectives of fulfilling generation of energy especially from coals and fossil fuel-based energy and keeping carbon footprints low. But if India completely abandons the carbon credit policy it could face backlash from the international community on the issue of climate change. Hence instead of completely abandoning carbon credit policy India needs to moderate it policy as per global demand and domestic energy demands.

## Question 146 (Year: 2014 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

**Question ID: 2014-gs3-q146-unacademy**
**Q15. Environmental Impact Assessment studies are increasinglyundertakenbeforeaprojectiscleared by the Government. Discuss the environmental impacts of coal-fired thermal plants located at coal pitheads. (250 Words, 15 marks) Tag: Conservation, Environmental Pollution and Degradation, Environmental Impact Assessment.**

#

## Answer

## **Decoding the Question**

- **In intro try to, define the concept of EIA and** **legal backing in India**-**In Body,**-**Discuss first part as impact of coal-fired** **thermal power plant located at pithead.**-**Trytoconcludewithsuggestionswithrespect** **to environmental conservation.** **Answer:**An environmental impact assessment (EIA) is commonly described as an assessment of the impact of planned activities on the environment, including impacts on biodiversity, vegetation and ecology, water, and air. An EIA can be seen as a process of identifying, predicting, and evaluating the likely environmental, socioeconomic, cultural, and other impacts of a proposed project or development to define mitigation actions—not only to reduce negative impacts but also to provide positive contributions to the natural environment and well-being.**Legal provisions backing Environment Impact**

## **Assessment (EIA) in India**

- Until 1994, environmental clearance from the Central Government was an administrative decision and lacked legislative support. EIA was mademandatoryin1994,undertheEnvironmental Protection Act of 1986 which contains various provisions on EIA methodology and process.
- The Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change (MoEFCC) notified new EIA legislation in September 2006. The notification makes it mandatory for various projects such as mining, thermal power plants, river valley, infrastructure (road, highway, ports, harbours and airports) and industries including very small electroplating or foundry units to get environment clearance. However, unlike the EIA Notification of 1994, the new legislation has put the onus of clearing projects on the state government depending on the size/capacity of the project. **Coal powered thermal plants at the Pithead:**Coal is the one of the natural resources and fossil fuel abundance In India which is used by thermal power plants for electricity generation to match demand of energy in India. Due to high ash content in Indian coal, emphasis is being laid now on setting up coal fired Super, Ultra and Mega Power Projects on pithead itself in order to minimize cost associated with bulk transport of ash laden coal. But it has caused several environmental challenges related to pollution at the local level.**Environmental impact of Coal powered thermal**

## **plants at the Pithead**

- Air Pollution: It includes sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, particulate matter (PM), and heavy metals, leading to smog, acid rain, toxins in the environment. For pithead thermal power plants located in deep remote forested areas, it disrupts entire biodiversity, causing respiratory, cardiovascular, and cerebrovascular effects in animal and human beings.
- Ash in air gets deposited on nearby agriculture fieldswhichagainbecomeproblemsforthenatural process of photosynthesis. Due to deposition of ash on crops it may enter into food chains of humans as well.
- Pollution in surface water resources. Water slurry from coal fired thermal power plants may be transported to ash ponds for disposal. It also contains harmful metals such as boron, lead arsenic etc. which can be very dangerous for local populations with respect to public health.
- Impact on soil can be seen as soil in nearby areas of coal pithead become alkaline due to the alkaline nature of ash. This will have a negative impact on agricultural land as they are very harmful to crop production.Eventhismayleadtobioaccumulation of heavy metals pollution.
- Coal combustion waste disposed of in landfills or “surface impoundments,” are another concern. As rain filters through the toxic ash pits year after year, the toxic metals are leached out into the local environment.
- Acid mine drainage (AMD): Which refers to the outflow of acidic water from coal mines or metal mines, often abandoned mines where ore- or coal mining activities have exposed rocks containing the sulphur-bearing mineral pyrite. Pyrite reacts with air and water to form sulphuric acid and dissolved iron, and as water washes through mines, this compound forms a dilute acid, which can wash into nearby rivers and streams, making them acidic adversely impacting river ecology. While India is planning to shift to more and more environmentally friendly clean sources of energy, presently coal-fired power plants continue to be India’s main source for electricity generation. In such a situation, Environment Impact assessment comes as a handy preventive tool evaluating and mitigating environmental impact of such proposed coal fired power plants. Such assessment aims at solving many of theseproblemsintheplanningphaseitself.Itsstudyon mitigationrecommendstheactionstoreduceandavoid the potential adverse environmental consequences, followed by reporting to the decision-making body and a follow-up on adequacy and effectiveness of the EIA report. It also has a post monitoring stage, which comes into play once the project is commissioned. It checks to ensure that the impacts of the project do not exceed the legal standards and implementation of the mitigation measures are in the manner as described in the EIA report.

## Question 147 (Year: 2013 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

## Answer

The project is aimed at synchronizing electricity produced from renewable sources (such as solar and wind) with conventional power stations in the grid. Germany has committed developmental and technical assistance of € 1 billion (US$ 1.33 billion) for the project. The project can be expectedtostrengthenthepowerdistributionnetwork in India. The Green Energy Corridor project can be expected to result in the development of an integrated grid across the nation by making its grid compatible for distributing renewable energy.

## **Problems in India’s conventional energy**

- **Climate Change:** The Sources of Conventional energy are oil, Gas , and Coal, which are usually called Fossil Fuels. The conventional form of energy raises concerns about climate change and is a challenge to meet India’s Paris Climate commitment under Intended Nationally Determined Contributions (INDC).
- **Import Bill:** Conventional energy increases import dependence and this import dependence increases forex burden. According to provisional data from Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), in FY20 India’s oil import bill slipped to $ 101.4 billion from a level of $ 111.9 billion in the previous fiscal FY 2019.

- **IndoorPollution:InmostofIndia’svillages,wood,**cow dung, and other traditional forms of energy resources are still used to heat and lighten up their home. This resulted in increased indoor pollution which is a serious health concern.**Green Corridor Resolves Conventional Energy**

## **Problems**

- **Different Voltage:** At present, the National Grid confronts trouble in engrossing sustainable power sources because of differing voltage and supply. The aim is to make the transmission framework dynamic to deal with the variations in voltage. Germany’s technological help would be pivotal in this project since it has keen networks which can incorporate sustainable power sources into its national matrix.
- **Future Proof:** India has an expected 28000 MW of Installed sustainable power source capacity. Bringing this into the national grid needs overhauling of the overall national grid. The National Green corridor will help in the smooth transfer of power in this grid system.
- **Connecting Roof-Top:** Rooftop solar energy production has been given a boost by government policies. This increasing rooftop solar power production needs to be connected to the state or national grid, and the green energy corridor will help to reduce this issue.
- **Help to Achieve Targets:** As the government has set targets of 175 GW renewable energy in which solarandwindhaveasignificantchunk.Toconnect them to the national grid is essential and this NGC will help in fastening targets achievements.
- **Reserving Coal Deposits:** NGC will contribute to reducing dependence on coal for thermal energy generation hence, India may potentially keep reserves of coal for future generations. Thus, it is said that India’s green energy corridor will not only help in connecting green energy from different parts of the country but also, it will have multiple impacts on India’s green energy generation and distribution in different parts of the country.

## **Consequences of illegal mining**

## Question 149 (Year: 2013 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

**Question ID: 2013-gs3-q149-unacademy**
**Q 20. Enumerate the National Water Policy of India. Taking river Ganges as an example, discuss the strategies which may be adopted for river water pollution control and management. What are the legal provisions for management and handling of hazardous wastes in India? (200 Words, 10 Marks) Tag: Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment.**

#

## Answer

## **Decoding the Question**

- **In the Intro try to write about India’s river** **pollution.**-**In Body,**-**Discuss the strategies for controlling** **and management of river pollution.**-**In the second part of the answer** **legal provisions for management and** **handling hazardous waste.**-**In Conclusion, try to write about the need** **for river pollution.** **Answer:**India is one of the worst countries affected by river pollution as with nearly 70% of water being contaminated, India is placed 120th amongst 122 countries in the water quality index. The Ganga river holds deep religious significance in India with thousands thronging the Ganga’s ghats (banks) every year to bathe and offer prayers. But the alarming levels of pollutants and sewage waste that are discharged into it every day by over 1100 industrial units and several towns situated on its banks, have made it one of the most polluted rivers in the world. Water of river Ganga, which is considered as nectar in India, has become poisonous today. What to talk of drinking, it cannot even be used for bathing. A dangerous virus named Bacteriophage is found in the Ganga.**Strategies Need to be Adopted:** The following guiding principles provide a suitable basis for sound management of water pollution.
- **PreventPollutionRatherThanTreatingSymptoms** **of Pollution:Although** wastewater treatment facilitieshavebeeninstalledandimprovedoverthe years in many countries, water pollution remains a problem, including in industrialised countries.
- In some situations, the introduction of improved wastewater treatment has only led to increased pollution from other media, such as wastewater sludge.
- **Use the Precautionary Principle:** There are many examples of the application and discharge of hazardous substances into the aquatic environment, even when such substances are suspected of having detrimental effects on the environment.
- Until now the use of any substance and its release to the environment has been widely accepted unless scientific research has proved unambiguously a causal link between the substance and a well-defined environmental impact.
- **Apply the Polluter-Pays-Principle:** The polluterpays-principle, where the costs of pollution prevention, control and reduction measures are borne by the polluter, is not a new concept but has not yet been fully implemented, despite the fact that it is widely recognised that the perception of water as a free commodity can no longer be maintained.
- **Apply Realistic Standards and Regulations:** Unrealistic standards and non-enforceable regulations may do more harm than having no standards and regulations, because they create an attitude of indifference towards rules and regulations in general, both among polluters and administrators.
- **Balance Economic and Regulatory Instruments:** Until now, regulatory management instruments have been heavily relied upon by governments in most countries for controlling water pollution. Economic instruments, typically in the form of wastewater discharge fees and fines, have been introduced to a lesser extent and mainly by industrialised countries.
- **Apply Water Pollution Control at the Lowest** **Appropriate Level:**The appropriate level may be defined as the level at which significant impacts are experienced. If environmental impact affects a neighbouring community, then the appropriate management level is one level higher than the community level, for example the river basin level.**Legal Provisions for Handling Hazardous Wastes:** Hazardous waste means any waste, which by reason of characteristics, such as physical, chemical, biological, reactive, toxic, flammable, explosive or corrosive, causes danger to health, or environment.
- In exercise of the powers conferred by sections 6, 8 and 25 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 (29 of 1986), the Central Government rules to protect the environment. The Hazardous Wastes (Management and Handling) Rules, 1989 were notified under the provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. The salient features of Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management & Transboundary Movement) Rules,

## **2016**

- Waste Management hierarchy in the sequence of priority of prevention, minimization, reuse, recycling, recovery, co-processing; and safe disposal has been incorporated.
- All the forms under the rules for permission, import/export, filing of annual returns, transportation, etc. have been revised significantly, indicating the stringent approach for management of such hazardous and other wastes with simultaneous simplification of procedure.
- The basic necessity of infrastructure to safeguard thehealthandenvironmentfromwasteprocessing industry has been prescribed as Standard Operating Procedure (SOPs), specific to waste type, which has to be complied by the stakeholders and ensured by SPCB/PCC while granting such authorisation.
- Procedure has been simplified to merge all the approvals as a single window clearance for setting up of hazardous waste disposal facility and import of other wastes. **The Hazardous Substances Management Division** **(HSMD)** is the nodal point for management of chemical emergencies and hazardous substances in India. The Division is also the nodal point for the following four International Conventions viz.
- BaselConventiononControloftransboundary movement of Hazardous waste and their disposal.
- Rotterdam Convention on Prior Informed Consent Procedure for certain Chemicals and Pesticides in International trade.
- Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants.
- The Minamata Convention on Mercury and StrategicApproachtoInternationalChemicals Management. **National Inventory of Hazardous Wastes:** The Ministry has also initiated a project on GIS Based National Hazardous Waste Information System.
- It is a web-based system, which has been developedtoprovidestatusofhazardouswaste management in the Country. The database available on the web is required to be regularly updated by all State Pollution Control Boards to ensure updated status at all times. Through NHWIS, a survey of 33,000 hazardous waste industries and MIS data entry of about 27,500 hazardous waste industries has been completed. However, in India still river pollution has been a very critical issue. All the components of physical environments must be protected from the pollution. Hence river pollution and hazardous pollution is the real problem which needs to be tackled very efficiently, which should make all the rivers a source of sustainable development. The key is to implement laws and regulations in their true spirit.

## Question 150 (Year: 2024 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

**Question ID: 2024-gs3-q150-unacademy**
**Q5.What is the present world scenario of intellectual property rights with respect to life materials? Although, India is second in the world to file patents, still only a few have been commercialized. Explain the reasons behind this less commercialization. (150 Words, 10 Marks)**

#

## Answer

**Answer:** **Introduction:**Intellectual property (IP) laws protect creators’ rights, enabling them to earn recognition or financial benefits from their inventions. The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), a UN agency, ensures global innovators’ ideas are protected and successfully reach the market to benefit society.**Global trends and controversies in patenting with**

## **respect to life materials**

- Globally, there has been a surge in patent filings related to life materials (biotechnology, genetics, pharmaceuticals). Countries like the USA and China lead in patenting genetic material, GMOs, and pharmaceutical products.
- Patentability of life materials, especially genes and living organisms, has been controversial. Ethical concerns arise over patenting life forms, with debates on bio-piracy and traditional knowledge exploitation.
- Intellectual property is governed globally by agreements such as TRIPS (Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights) under the WTO, which mandates member countries to adopt IPR regimes for life sciences, including pharmaceuticals and biotechnology. WIPOs World Intellectual Property Indicators 2023 (WIPI) report observed that patent applications in India grew by 31.6 per cent in 2022, “extending an 11year run of growth unmatched by any other country among the top 10 filers”. With a focus on affordable healthcare and biotechnology, India has made significant progress in filing patents for new drugs, agricultural innovations, and genetic research.

## **Reasons for less commercialisation**

- **Missing link Industry-Academia:** Due to this weak linkage innovations remain confined to laboratories and fail to find industrial partners to develop them into marketable products.
- **Limited Investment and Funding:** Indian startups and firms often lack the venture capital or government support needed to bring life-material patents into production.
- **Complex Regulatory Environment:** India’s regulatoryframeworkforbiotech,pharma,andlife materials is often seen as cumbersome and slow. Clearance processes for drugs, medical devices, or genetically modified organisms (GMOs) are lengthy, discouraging commercialization.
- **Absence of Technology Transfer Infrastructure:**The lack of established technology transfer sops in universities and research institutions hinders the process of taking patents from labs to industries.**Conclusion:** The Indian government has increased efforts to strengthen the collaboration between industries and research labs. However, the high level of technological maturity demanded by the market is difficult to achieve within academic settings due to funding and other challenges. Innovation needs to extend beyond product development and must also focus on the business side to ensure market success.

## Question 151 (Year: 2024 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

**Question ID: 2024-gs3-q151-unacademy**
**Q6.What is the technology being employed for electronic toll collection on highways? What are its advantages and limitations? What are the proposed changes that will make this process seamless? Would this transition carry any potential hazards? (150 Words, 10 Marks)**

#

## Answer

**Answer:** **Introduction:**India currently employs , a Radio Frequency**FASTag** Identification (RFID) passive tag, for electronic toll collection.

- FASTag is affixed on a vehicle’s windshield and is linkedtoaprepaidaccount,allowingtollpayments to be deducted automatically as vehicles pass through toll plazas.
- This technology reduces the need for stopping at toll booths, improving traffic flow. **Body:**:**Advantages of FASTag**-**Time-saving:** Vehicles no longer need to stop for cash payments, which helps reduce congestion at toll plazas.
- : It cuts down the need for cash **Cost-effective** handling and speeds up transactions.
- :Fastertrafficmovement **Environmentallyfriendly** reduces fuel consumption and emissions.
- **Transparency:** It ensures transparency in toll payments and reduces leakage in revenue collection.

## **Limitations of FASTag**

- **Scanner issues:** Often, the automatic scanners fail, requiringmanualscanningwithhandhelddevices, causing delays.
- **Misplaced or multiple tags:** Incorrectly placed FASTags or vehicles with multiple tags confuse scanners, further disrupting traffic flow.
- **Lackofuniformity:Thesystemisnotyetseamless,** leading to complaints of inefficiency and long wait times at toll plazas.

## **Proposed Changes**

- The government plans to introduce **GPS-based** **toll collection**using**Global Navigation Satellite** **System (GNSS)** technology.
- This system will calculate tolls based on the distancetravelledbyvehicles,eliminatingtheneed for toll plazas altogether.
- Vehicles will be equipped with an **On-Board Unit** **(OBU)** to track their coordinates, and tolls will be deducted from linked digital wallets.

## **Advantages of GPS-based Toll Collection**

- **Barrier-free tolling:** No need for toll booths, allowing for seamless travel and reducing traffic congestion.
- **Distance-based charges:** Charges will be more accurate, based on the actual distance covered by a vehicle.
- **Enhanced transparency:** The GPS system can provide real-time data on traffic patterns, helping improve road management.

## **Potential Hazards**

- **Technological** **readiness:** Implementing a nationwide system requires upgrading infrastructure and ensuring the accuracy of GNSS devices.
- **Old vehicle adaptation:** Retrofitting older vehicles with OBUs may be challenging and costly.
- **Data privacy and security:** With GPS tracking, concerns over data misuse and direct debit from bank accounts need to be addressed.
- **Initial chaos:**A swift transition may create confusion among drivers, similar to the early days of FASTag implementation.**Conclusion:**Thus, the**GPS-based toll system** promises a more efficient and seamless process, its success depends on careful implementation, infrastructure upgrades, and addressing privacy concerns. Overcoming these challenges could revolutionise India’s toll collection, reducing travel times and enhancing the overall efficiency of the highway network.

**Answer:** **Introduction:**The Digital Personal Data Protection Act ,2023 provides for the**processing of digital personal data**in a manner that recognizes both the rights of the individuals to protect their personal data and the need to process such personal data for lawful purposes and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.Personal data is information that relates to an identified or identifiable individual. ## **Act, 2023**

- Defines personal data and sensitive personal data.
- Establishes principles for processing personal data, including consent, purpose limitation, and storage limitation.
- Requires data fiduciaries (entities collecting personal data) to undertake certain duties like implementing security safeguards and data protection impact assessments.
- Provides rights to individuals/data principles such as the right to access, correction, and erasure of their personal data.
- Mandates data breach notifications and establishes a Data Protection Authority to oversee compliance and handle grievances, and enforce penalties for violations.
- It also applies to non-citizens living in India whose data processing “in connection with any activity related to offering of goods or services” happens outside India.
- TheActgrantsthegovernmentbroaddiscretionary powers to exempt certain businesses from compliance requirements. It also allows significant exceptions for state activities, particularly in emergencies or matters of national security. **Conclusion:** Data (Digital personal data) is the new oil. ## Question 154 (Year: 2024 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

**Question ID: 2024-gs3-q154-unacademy**
**Q16.What are asteroids? How real is the threat of them causing the extinction of life? What strategies have been developed to prevent such a catastrophe? (Answer in 250 words, 15 Marks)**

#

## Answer

**Answer:** **Introduction:** **Asteroids,** sometimes called minor planets, are rocky, airless remnants left over from the early formation of our solar system about 4.6 billion years ago. Most asteroids can be found orbiting the Sun between Mars and Jupiter within the main asteroid belt. Although most asteroids pose no threat to Earth, some follow trajectories that bring them close to our planet.

## **Categorization of Asteroids**

- **Main Asteroid Belt:** Asteroids orbiting between Mars and Jupiter. This contains the majority of known asteroids and is estimated to have 1 to 2 million asteroids.
<p align="center"><img src="images/unacademy_p66_img98.png" alt="Diagram" /></p>

- **Trojan Asteroids:** Asteroids share an orbit with a larger planet. The Trojan Asteroids do not collide with the planet because of where the Trojan asteroids orbit the sun in relation to the parent planet.
- **Near-Earth Asteroids (NEAs):** These asteroids pass close to Earth. About 10,000 NEAs have been discovered to date. And over 1,400 have been classified as Potentially Hazardous Asteroids or PHAs.
- NEAs are further divided into groups (Atira, Aten, Apollo and Amor).

## **Threat of Extinction from Asteroid Impacts**

- While asteroid impacts of this magnitude are rare, they are not impossible.
- Statistically, impacts from smaller objects (a few metres wide) are more frequent but tend to burn up in Earth’s atmosphere.
- ISRO Chairman Dr. S. Somanath warned that Asteroidslargerthan300metreshavethepotential to cause continental-scale devastation.
- Inaworst-casescenario,acollisionwithanasteroid of this magnitude could lead to catastrophic consequences, including mass extinction.
- Dr.Somanathemphasisedtheimportanceofbeing prepared for all possibilities.
- “Whiletheseeventsmaynotoccurwithinahuman lifespan, we must not take them for granted. We need to develop technology that allows us to predict and prevent such occurrences,” he said.
- The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has issued a warning about a potentially hazardous asteroid named Apophis, which is set to pass dangerously close to Earth on April 13, 2029.
- This asteroid, named after the Egyptian God of Chaos, has garnered attention due to its massive size and the potential for devastation if it were to collide with the planet.
- ISRO’s Network for Space Objects Tracking and Analysis (NETRA) is closely monitoring the asteroid’s trajectory.
- Dr. A K Anil Kumar, who leads NETRA, added that a collision with an asteroid like Apophis could cause “global disruption.”
- He cited a historical precedent: the Lonar Crater in Maharashtra, created by a meteor strike over 500,000 years ago, serves as a reminder of the power of such events.
- **Past Asteroid Incidents** The Earth has faced threats from space before.
- In 2013, a 20-metre asteroid exploded over Oblast, Russia, injuring 1,500 people and damaging thousands of buildings.
- The 1908 Tunguska event, caused by a 30-metre asteroid, levelled 80 million trees in Siberia.
- However,themostdevastatingasteroidimpact occurred approximately 650 million years ago in Mexico, wiping out the dinosaurs and 70% of Earth’s species.

## **Strategies Developed to Prevent a Catastrophe**

- **Global Collaboration on Planetary Defense:** The threat posed by Apophis has spurred international efforts to develop asteroid deflection technologies. NASA, in collaboration with other space agencies, is working on multiple missions to address this challenge.
- **ISRO’s Network for Space Objects Tracking and** **Analysis (NETRA)** also monitors the asteroid’s trajectory.
- **TheOSIRIS-RExspacecraft,originallydesignedto** return asteroid samples, has now been redirected to study Apophis.
- Additionally, the European Space Agency is consideringlaunchingtheRapidApophisMission **for Security and Safety (RAMSES)** in 2028 to further understand the asteroid’s trajectory.
- **Deflection Strategies:**Several strategies have been proposed to prevent a catastrophic collision with Earth. NASA successfully tested its**Double** **Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission,** which demonstrated the possibility of changing an asteroid’s course by directly impacting it with a spacecraft.
- Other options include using gravity tractors to nudge the asteroid away.
- **GravityTractors:Thisconceptinvolvesplacing** a spacecraft near an asteroid. The gravitational attraction between the spacecraft and the asteroid, over time, would pull the asteroid into a new trajectory, away from Earth.
- However, in an extreme scenario, **nuclear** **explosives**may be considered to break up the asteroid.**Conclusion:** While the threat of an extinction-level asteroid impact remainslow,it isnot negligible.Advancesindetection, monitoring, and deflection technologies have greatly improved our ability to prevent such catastrophes. Continued investment in planetary defence is crucial to safeguarding humanity from these potentially devastating natural events.

## Question 157 (Year: 2023 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

**Question ID: 2023-gs3-q157-unacademy**
**Q16. What is the main task of India’s third moon mission which could not be achieved in its earlier mission?Listthecountriesthathaveachievedthis task. Introduce the subsystems in the spacecraft launched and explain the role of the ‘Virtual Launch Control Centre’ at the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre which contributed to the successful launch from Sriharikota. (15 Marks, 250 Words)**

#

## Answer

## **Approach**

- **Begin with an introduction** – Briefly mention Chandrayaan-3andIndia’slunarprogramme.

## **Body**

- **State the main task** – Highlight the primary objective that failed in Chandrayaan-2 but was achieved in Chandrayaan-3.
- **List countries** – Mention the four countries that have achieved soft lunar landing, with timelines.
- **Explain subsystems** – Break down the propulsion module, lander, rover, and support systems.
- **Describe VLCC’s role** – Explain how digital monitoring and redundancy enhanced the launch.
- **Conclude** – Stress the significance of Chandrayaan-3 for India’s global space standing.

## **Answer**

**Introduction:**India’s**Chandrayaan-3 mission (2023)**was launched by LVM3-M4 from Sriharikota to demonstrate advanced space technology capabilities. It followed Chandrayaan-2 (2019), which successfully reached lunar orbit but failed in its final descent due to a lander guidance issue.

##**Main Task of Chandrayaan-3**

- The mission’s**primary objective was to achieve a** **soft landing** on the Moon, which Chandrayaan-2 could not accomplish.
- This task was critical as a soft landing enables insitu experiments, rover deployment, and longterm exploration.
- The landing was successfully achieved on **23rd** **August 2023,**making India the first country to reach the**lunar south pole region,** an area rich in water-ice deposits and minerals.

## **Countries that Achieved Soft Lunar Landing**

- **Soviet Union (1966):** Achieved the first-ever soft landing with its Luna 9 mission.
- **United States (1966):** Followed with Surveyor missions and later Apollo crewed landings.
- **China (2013):** Landed Chang’e-3 and later Chang’e-4 on the far side of the Moon.
- **India (2023):**With Chandrayaan-3, became the**fourth nation**and the**first at the south pole** to master this complex technology.
<p align="center"><img src="images/unacademy_p154_img91.png" alt="Diagram" /></p>

## **Subsystems in the Chandrayaan-3 Spacecraft**

- **Vikram Lander:**The lander was built to execute a**controlled soft landing**on the Moon’s surface. It is designed to study**lunar topography, thermal** **properties, and mineral composition,** providing crucialinsightsintotheMoon’ssouthpolarregion.
- **Lander Payloads:****RAMBHA-LP** **(Langmuir** **Probe):**Designed to measure the near-surface plasma (ions and electrons) density and study its variation over time. Thishelpsinunderstandinghowthelunar environment interacts with solar wind. **ChaSTE (Chandra’s Surface Thermo-** **physical** **Experiment):**Conducts measurements of the thermal properties of lunar surface soil in the polar region. It provides insights into how heat is stored and transmitted on the Moon. **ILSA (Instrument for Lunar Seismic** **Activity):** Records seismic activity around the landing site and maps the structure of the lunar crust and mantle. This helps assess the Moon’s tectonic behaviour and internal layering.
- **Rover (Pragyan):** Six-wheeled, solar-powered vehicleequippedwithAPXSandLIBSinstruments for elemental analysis of lunar soil and rocks.
- **Rover Payloads:****APXS** **(Alpha** **Particle** **X-Ray** **Spectrometer):**Determines the elemental composition of lunar soil and rocks (Mg, Al, Si, K, Ca, Ti, Fe). This enhances knowledge about the chemical diversity at the landing site. **LIBS (Laser Induced Breakdown** **Spectroscope):** Derives chemical composition and mineralogical properties of the lunar surface by firing laser pulses. It deepens understanding of lunar crust evolution.
- **Propulsion Module:** Carried the lander to lunar orbit and housed the SHAPE payload, designed to study Earth-like exoplanets.
- **Propulsion Module Payload:****SHAPE** **(Spectro-polarimetry** **of** **HabitablePlanetEarth):** Anexperimental payload to study the spectro-polarimetric signaturesofEarthasahabitableplanet. It observes Earth in the near-infrared (1–1.7 µm) to assist future exoplanet habitability studies.
- **Deep Space Network (DSN):**A strong communication system links Chandrayaan-3 with Earth stations. ISRO was supported by**NASA’s** **DSN,** which offered real-time tracking, telemetry relay, and command support, crucial for deepspace navigation.
- **SolarX-rayMonitor(SXM):Anonboardscientific**instrument used to record X-ray emissions from the Sun. It enhances understanding of the**Moon’s** **mineral composition** by studying how solar radiation interacts with the lunar surface.

## **Role of the Virtual Launch Control Centre (VLCC)**

- The VLCC at Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC), Thiruvananthapuram functioned as a digital twin of the launch control room at Sriharikota.
- It enabled **remote monitoring and real-time** **analysis** of thousands of rocket health parameters across geographically separated teams.
- The centre provided **redundancy and backup** **support** in case of local system failures at Sriharikota.
- Itensuredsecurecommunicationlinksforsharing simulation data, telemetry, and decision-making inputs among scientists.
- This innovation enhanced **efficiency, safety, and** **coordination,**making Chandrayaan-3’s launch highly reliable.**Conclusion:**Chandrayaan-3achievedIndia’slong-pendingobjective**ofasuccessfullunarsoftlanding,strengtheningIndia’s**globalspaceleadership.ThemissionhighlightedIndia’s ability to develop**indigenous subsystems and digital** **innovations like VLCC,** showing how technology integration can ensure future success in deep-space exploration.

As the successor to the Hubble Space Telescope, JWST possesses unique features that set it apart from its predecessors, with the potential to transform our understanding of the universe.**Body:** **Unique Features:** **Infrared Observations:**JWST is specifically designed to operate in the infrared spectrum, providing enhanced capabilities to observe distant objects and events, such as the formation of galaxies and the birth of stars, which are obscured by dust clouds in visible light.**Larger Mirror:**With a 6.5-meter primary mirror, JWST’slight-gatheringcapabilitysurpassestheHubble Space Telescope’s 2.4-meter mirror, enabling more detailed observations and imaging of celestial objects.**Sunshield:**JWST is equipped with a five-layer sunshield to protect its sensitive instruments from the Sun’s heat, ensuring stable and precise observations at extremely low temperatures.**Orbiting Position:**JWST is positioned in an orbit around the second Lagrange point (L2), located about 1.5 million kilometres from Earth. This strategic location minimizes interference from Earth’s thermal radiation and allows for continuous observations.**Key Goals of the Mission:** **Understanding Early Universe:**JWST aims to study the first galaxies that formed after the Big Bang, providing insights into the early universe’s structure and evolution.**Star and Planet Formation:**The telescope will investigatetheformationofstarsandplanetswithinour galaxy and beyond, shedding light on the conditions necessary for life to emerge.**Exoplanet Characterization:**JWST will analyze the atmospheres of exoplanets, potentially identifying signs of habitability or even extraterrestrial life.**GalaxyEvolution:Thetelescope’sadvancedcapabilities**will allow scientists to study the evolution of galaxies, understanding their growth and interaction over cosmic time.**Potential Benefits for the Human Race:** **Scientific Discoveries:**JWST’s unprecedented observations could lead to groundbreaking scientific discoveries, revolutionizing our understanding of the universe and our place in it.**Technological Advancement:**The development of JWST has pushed the boundaries of space technology, inspiring new innovations and applications that may benefit various industries and space exploration missions.**Inspiration and Education:**JWST’s stunning images and scientific findings have the potential to inspire future generations of scientists, astronomers, and space enthusiasts, fostering interest in science and technology.**Search for Extraterrestrial Life:**The telescope’s exoplanet studies may provide critical information in thesearchforhabitableplanetsandextraterrestriallife, answeringoneofhumanity’smostprofoundquestions.**Examples:**JWST’s advanced infrared imaging capabilities have already captured unprecedented images of distant galaxies, showcasing its potential for groundbreaking discoveries in astrophysics. The telescope’s study of exoplanet atmospheres may pave the way for identifying potentially habitable worlds and revolutionize our understanding of exoplanetary systems.**Conclusion:** The James Webb Space Telescope’s unique features, ambitious goals, and potential benefits make it a trailblazing instrument in the realm of space exploration and astrophysics. With its unparalleled capabilities, JWST holds the promise of unlocking the mysteries of the cosmos, inspiring future generations, and contributing to the advancement of human knowledge and technology. Its successful mission represents a remarkable achievement for humanity’s quest to understand the universe and our place in it.

## Question 159 (Year: 2022 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

**Question ID: 2022-gs3-q159-unacademy**
**16. What is the basic principle behind vaccine development? How do vaccines work? What approaches were adopted by the Indian vaccine manufacturers to produce COVID-19 vaccines ? (Answer in 250 words) 15 Marks Approach**

#

## Answer

- **Introduction:** Write about general ideas behind vaccine development.

## **Body**

- Mention Basic Principle of Vaccine Development and how it works.
- Write Indian Vaccine Manufacturers’ Approaches for COVID-19 Vaccine.
- **Conclusion:**Conclude the answer summarising the points mentioned.**Answer:** **Introduction:**Vaccine development is based on the principle of introducing a weakened or inactivated form of a pathogen or a specific component of it into the body to stimulate the immune system. Vaccines work by priming the immune system to recognize and remember the pathogen, enabling a rapid and effective response if the individual is exposed to the actual infection. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Indian vaccine manufacturers played a crucial role in producing COVID-19 vaccines using different approaches to combat the virus.**Body:** **Basic Principle of Vaccine Development:**Vaccines are designed to mimic the presence of a pathogen in the body without causing the disease. They contain antigens, which are components of the pathogen, such as weakened or inactivated viruses or specific proteins.**How Vaccines Work:**When a vaccine is administered, the antigens in the vaccine stimulate the immune system to produce a response, triggering the production of antibodies and memory cells. If the vaccinated individual encounters the actual pathogen later, the immune system recognizes it and mounts a swift and targeted response, preventing the development of the disease or reducing its severity.**Indian Vaccine Manufacturers’ Approaches for**

## **COVID-19 Vaccines**

**a. Covaxin by Bharat Biotech:**Covaxin is an inactivated virus-based vaccine. Bharat Biotech inactivated the SARS-CoV-2 virus and used it as an antigen to stimulate an immune response in the recipients.It was one of the first COVID-19 vaccines to be developed and manufactured in India, playing a significant role in the country’s vaccination drive.**b. CovishieldbySerumInstituteofIndia:Covishield**is a viral vector-based vaccine. The vaccine uses a weakened version of a different virus (adenovirus) as a vector to deliver the genetic instructions for the spike protein of SARS-CoV-2, stimulating an immune response. Covishield, based on the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine, has been widely used in India and other countries under the COVAX initiative.**c. Sputnik V by Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories:**Sputnik V is also a viral vector-based vaccine. It uses two different adenoviruses (Ad26 and Ad5) to deliver the genetic instructions for the spike protein of SARS-CoV-2. Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories collaborated with the Russian Gamaleya Research Institute to produce and distribute Sputnik V in India.**d. Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine by Serum Institute** **of India:**It is a protein subunit vaccine. It contains a small piece of the spike protein of SARS-CoV-2 as an antigen to trigger an immune response. Serum Institute of India partnered with Novavax to manufacture the protein subunit vaccine candidate for India and other low and middleincome countries.**Conclusion:** Indian vaccine manufacturers have played a crucial role in producing COVID-19 vaccines using different approaches, such as inactivated virus, viral vector-based, and protein subunit vaccines. Their contributions have been instrumental in accelerating thevaccinationdriveinIndiaandglobally,contributing to the fight against the COVID-19 pandemic.

## Question 160 (Year: 2021 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

**Question ID: 2021-gs3-q160-unacademy**
**Q5. How is S-400 air defence system technically superior to any other system presently available in the world? (10 Marks, 150 Words) Tags: Achievements of Indians in Science and Technology**

#

## Answer

## **Decoding the Question**

- **Introduction:Giveabriefintroductionabout** **the S-400 air defence system.**

## **Body**

- **Mention how the S-400 air defence** **system is technically superior to any** **other system presently available in the** **world with examples.**-**Conclusion: Conclude suitably.** **Answer:** Russia has developed the mobile surface-to-air missile (SAM)systemknownastheS-400Triumf.Itisregarded as one of the most cutting-edge air defence systems in the world, capable of simultaneously detecting and eliminating a variety of approaching aerial threats. It is regarded to be far more deadly than the US-developed Terminal High Altitude Area Defence (THAAD) system, making it the most dangerous operationally deployed modern long-range SAM (MLR SAM) in the world. Russia and India have signed a USD 5.43 billion contract for the supply of S-400 in October 2018.

## **Technical Superiority of S-400 Air Defence System**

- The S-400 Triumf can **simultaneously track and** **destroy** a variety of incoming objects, including aeroplanes,missiles,andunmannedaerialvehicles (UAV).
- Its **various coverage** envelopes range in size from 30 feet to one lakh feet above sea level and 40 kilometres to 400 kilometres in distance. Since practically no aerial aircraft in existence can reach beyond these ranges, this system provides protection from all potential threats.
- The entire system operates on its own and **doesn’t** **need human intervention** until absolutely necessary. Everything is automated, including the search, tracking, target recognition, transfer of target data over a secure link, evaluation of target parameters, and choice and launch of an appropriate counter-vehicle.
- This system not only has the ability to operate other Air Defense Systems available but also can share data with other systems placed nearby.

## **Advantage of S-400 over THAAD**

- The American THAAD is a one-dimensional missile system, in contrast to the Russian S-400, as it can only fire one type of missile up to a range of 150–200 km.
- S-400 can intercept a fighter jet, however THAAD cannot.

## **Advantage of S-400 over Patriot**

- Patriot is a combat-proven air defence system operated by the US and a number of its allies. Patriot has a range of 180 km.
- S-400 and Patriot take five and twenty-five minutes, respectively, to deploy.
- S-400’s maximum target speed is 4.8 km/s as opposed to Patriot’s 1.38 km/s.
- While S-400 is an anti-ballistic missile defence system, it can also engage other aerial targets including UAVs etc. There is a chance of a two-front engagement because India has two adversarial neighbours on its western and eastern frontiers. In view of this, even if the purchase of S-400 could result in US sanctions under CAATSA, it is essential for India’s strategic and tactical requirements.

## **Applied Biotechnology**

- Genetically engineered crops with increased nutritional value, pest resistance, and crop output are created via biotechnology. Bt cotton, GM soybeans, etc. are a few examples.
- Many drugs, like Insulin, are produced using recombinant DNA technology.
- Additionally, waste management and pollution reduction use biotechnology. As an illustration, phytoremediation employs plants to remove, degrade,orcontaintoxinsfromsoils,groundwater, etc.
- Biotechnology is used for the diagnosis of a number of diseases. For instance, RT-PCR is based on genetic amplification to detect the presence of viruses like Dengue, SARS, etc.

- IVF, test tube children, and other assisted reproductive technologies are all led by biotechnology. **RoleofAppliedBiotechnologyinUpliftingthePoorer**

## **Sections of Society**

- By boosting crop productivity and enhancing its resistance to pests and environmental changes, biotechnology is helping marginal farmers increase their income.
- It has revolutionised medical science, making world-class care and a regulated death rate achievable in India alone.
- Through genome sequencing, biotechnology provides access to data on people’s health from all around India, which ultimately helps the government create focused policy initiatives.
- Additionally, it helps food products remain on the market for longer, lowering their price for the underprivileged.
- The poor are particularly affected by pollution. Biotechnology lessens their suffering by assisting in the reduction of pollution. An example of when bioremediation is used is to clean landfills. The innovative field of biotechnology has the promise of reducing hunger and poverty. All social classes must receive an equitable share of its advantages, though.

## **sector**

## **Drug delivery system**

- **Nanoparticle drug delivery systems:** Utilizing degradableandabsorbablepolymers,providemore specificity to a particular site, thereby increasing the therapeutic efficiency more effectively and therefore can be used as effective transport and delivery systems.
- **Nanocapsules:** these are pods that encapsulate drugs, which ensures the drugs are released more slowly and steadily in the body
- **Dendrimers:** Tree-shaped synthetic nano molecules that carry drugs in the tips of the branches.
- **Nano bio magnets:** Nano bio magnets carry drugs for cancer, for instance, into the body and are held at the target site by an external magnet. The purpose of this is to concentrate the drug at the tumour site for long enough for it to be absorbed.
- Nanotechnology can also provide **alternatives to** **injectable vaccines** if the inactive virus is bound up with nanoparticles to increase the immune response.

## **In Disease Diagnosis**

- **Nanolitre systems** (known as lab-on-a-chip): These are devices that automate a biological process using fluids at the nanoliter scale.
- **Quantum dots:** Nanosized semiconductors can be used as biosensors to find disease because they fluoresce, they can be used to tag diseased cells.
- **Magnetic nanoparticles:** Magnetic nanoparticles can be used as Nanosensors.
- **Nanosensor arrays:** These are grids of nano sensors on silicon chips used in medical diagnosis. They provide a highly-sensitive, low-power, and compact tool for in-situ and real time analysis.
- **Antibody-dendrimer conjugates:** These are branched nano molecules with antibodies on their ends for diagnosis of HIV and cancer.
- **Nanoparticles as medical image enhancers:** Medical imaging relies on looking for contrasts in thewaylightisscatteredinhealthytissuecompared with diseased tissue. The sharper this contrast, the more accurate the diagnosis. Nanoparticles are able to give medical imaging techniques a sharper resolution, making it easier to identify disease.
- **Tuberculosis and Nanotechnology:** The Central Scientific Instruments Organisation of India has designed a nanotechnology-based TB diagnostic kit, currently undergoing clinical trials. This would cut both the cost and time required for TB tests and also require a smaller amount of blood for testing.

## **Uses in health Monitoring**

- Nanotubes and nanoparticles can be used as glucose, carbon dioxide and cholesterol sensors and for in-situ monitoring of homeostasis, the process by which the body maintains metabolic equilibrium.

## **Other Uses**

- Recently during pandemic, antiviral nano-coating on face masks and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits of healthcare workers to prevent them from COVID-19 infection.
- Nanopores are used in making DNA sequences more efficient. In India the government started a **National**. Advancement in the field of**Nanotechnology Mission** nanotechnology is very useful especially in the health care sector with respect to India. Nanotechnology and its application in the field of pharmaceuticals and medicines and various equipment have revolutionised the twentieth century. Nanotechnology is a valuable scientific revolution for the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of human diseases. Therefore, integral to modern healthcare especially in the times when infections can become pandemic.

## Question 167 (Year: 2019 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

**Question ID: 2019-gs3-q167-unacademy**
**Q15. How is the Government of India protecting traditional knowledge of medicine patenting by pharmaceutical companies? (250 Words 15 Marks) Tag: Awareness in the field of IT, Computer, Space, Robotics, Nanotechnology, and issues relating to intellectual property rights.**

#

## Answer

## **Decoding the Question**

- **InIntroduction,trytowriteabouttraditional** **knowledge of medicine.**-**In Body,**-**Mention the Indian scenario and issue** **related to it.**-**discuss various government steps for** **protecting traditional knowledge of** **medicine.**-**Conclude suggestions for protecting** **traditional knowledge.** **Answer:** Traditional knowledge (TK) is knowledge, knowhow, skills and practices that are developed, sustained and passed on from generation to generation within a community, often forming part of its cultural or spiritual identity. Thus, TK is a valuable yet vulnerable asset to indigenous and local communities who depend on TK for their livelihood. India has a rich culture and tradition of medicinal practice that dates back thousands of years. The healthcare needs of more than 70% population and livelihood of millions of people in India is dependent on traditional medicine. Recently, many multinational corporations aim to benefit from these traditional medicines. In order to protect the knowledge from being illegally patented, the government has indeed been striving hard to protect our heritage and well researched traditional knowledge.

## **Steps Taken**

- **TraditionalKnowledgeDigitalLibrary(TKDL):It** wasinitiatedinIndiain2001asadigitalrepository of TK. TKDL is proving to be an effective deterrent against bio-piracy.
- It is a pioneering Indian initiative to prevent exploitation and to protect Indian traditional knowledge from wrongful patents mainly at International Patent Offices.
- **Exclusive Ministry:** Ministry of AYUSH has been set up to protect, promote research in traditional medicinal knowledge, marketing and creating awareness for the same.
- **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage:** The government has successfully obtained recognition for its traditional medicine knowledge such as Ayurveda, Yoga, Sowa Rigpa, Unani, etc.
- It has helped India to establish links between countriesoforiginandpreventfilingofpatents by multinational pharma companies.
- **Funding:** To prevent research and knowledge of traditional medicine being leaked to private players only Centre Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) will carry research in this field.
- **Strengthening IPR regime:** In new norms there are provisions to protect traditional knowledge of cultural groups. The main aim behind it is to protect the economic interest of such groups from exploitation by third parties or from private players.
- **World Trade Organization:** India has been trying hard to restart negotiations on protecting traditional medicinal knowledge from being exploited by big corporations.
- **Nagoya protocol on benefit sharing:** India has signed and ratified Nagoya protocol on access to genetic resources and fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from their utilization. The protection of traditional medicinal knowledge is still a big challenge. The need is constant upgrading IPR rules, strengthening institutional mechanisms, improvement in vigilance and intelligence sharing among agencies are aiding the efforts.

## **Bose-Einstein Statistics**

- The Bose-Einstein distribution describes the statistical behaviour of integer spin particles (boson). At low temperature, bosons can behave verydifferentlythanfermionsbecauseanunlimited number of them can collect into the same energy state, a phenomenon called “condensation”.
- Physicist Paul Dirac was the first to use the term “boson”todescribetheparticlesthatobeyedBoseEinstein Statistics, in order to celebrate Bose’s contribution to developing this theory.
- In 1920 while working at Decca university he applied his statistical methods for counting photons.
- He sent his paper to Albert Einstein, he recognised the value of statistics. This paper turned into a seminal one and it is named after Bose-Einstein Statistics. **Bose-Einstein Statistics revolutionizing the field of**

## **Physics**

- It brought revolution in the field of Physics in following manner,
- It improved the standard model of particle physics.
- It helped in discovering the God particle by Peter Higgs. This discovery is contributing still to the field of

## **Physics in following manner**

- In 2013, Peter Higgs who won the Nobel prize for carrying out research using Bose-Einstein’s work wrote a paper about a very unstable particle that survives for a fraction of second after its birth and then it breaks apart producing other fundamental particles.
- It helped Peter Higgs in discovering the “God particle” or “Higgs Boson particle” which helped understanding the origin of the universe.
- The currently on-going research at CERN laboratory in Europe for discovering laboratorybased God particles. If scientists can discover this particle then it will further improve the standard model and understanding of our origin of the universe. Thus, the contribution made by Satyendra Nath Bose in discovering Bose-Einstein Statistics helped later on discovering the God Particle. Though he did not get the Nobel prize for his discovery, his contribution in this field is better than any award which changed fundamental understanding about the universe.

These stem cells can be procured from a lot of different sources and used to potentially treat more than approved 80 disorders. These are undifferentiated biological cells That can differentiate into specialized cells and divide to produce more stem cells. ## **types of treatments, like**

## Question 173 (Year: 2017 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

**Question ID: 2017-gs3-q173-unacademy**
**Q16. Give an account of the growth and development of nuclear science and technology in India. What is the advantage of fast breeder reactor programme in India? ( 250 Words, 15 Marks) Tag: Science and technology-developments and their application and effects in everyday life. Infrastructure: energy, ports, roads, airports, railways etc.**

#

## Answer

## **Decoding the Question**

- **InIntro,trytowriteaboutnucleartechnology** **and related information.**-**In Body,**-**Discuss India’s Three Stage Nuclear** **Energy Programme.**-**Discuss advantages of the Fast Breeder** **Reactor programme.**-**Try to conclude the answer by quoting NSG** **membership and climate change.** **Answer:**India’s pursuit for peaceful use of nuclear science and technology began with the vision of Dr Homi Bhabha’s. Initially, the Department of Atomic Energy (DEA) implemented India’s nuclear energy development programme till the creation of Nuclear Power Corporation of India (NPCIL). To extract energy from nuclear sources India adopted a**Three-** **stage Nuclear Power Development Programme**based on indigenously developed reactors and fuel processed from domestic resources.**Growth and Development of Nuclear Science and**

## **Technology**

- Establishment of **Department of Atomic Energy** **(DEA) in 1954.** DEA works under the direct charge of the Prime Minister. DAE’s primary responsibility was to make all technologies to harness nuclear energy, because all big nuclear power and technologically advanced countries denied technical assistance to India.
- , 410 MW at Tarapore **First Nuclear Power Plant** (Mumbai) Maharashtra, was set up with the 1963 Agreement between the USA and India .
- ThisisbasedonBoilingWaterReactortechnology by using enriched uranium fuel supplied by the USA.
- After 20 years of gap India signed an agreement with old ally, Soviet Union, for setting up of two nuclear power plants of thousand MW each which were based on **Pressurized Water Reactors** **technology,** at Kudankulam in Tamil Nadu.
- **The Three-stage Nuclear Power Programme:**It was formulated by Dr. Homi Bhabha in 1950’s to for India’s energy security and completely independent and harnessing nuclear energy, through the use of**uranium and thorium reserves** found in the monazite sands of coastal regions of Kerala.
- The three stages of nuclear power generation programme are in following manner:  **First stage:**Natural uranium fueled Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWR’s). This will use natural uranium from domestic sources as fuel and indigenously produced heavy water as both moderator and coolant. **Second stage:**Fast Breeder Reactors (FBR’s) for utilizing plutonium-based fuel, Plutonium -239, which is separated from spent fuel in the first stage, was to be used in indigenously developed fast breeder reactors (FBR’s) for generating electricity. **Thirdstage:** Itisbasedonbreederreactors using indigenously available thorium raw material from sea sands from southern coastal states and produces U-233 which in turn would be the fuel for electricity generation. Fast breeder reactors, or FBRs, in general produce more fissile material than they consume. Currently, all thecomponentsandequipment havebeensuccessfully manufactured by Indian industries. By following this approach, India has mastered the design and manufacturingofsodiumcooledFastBreederReactors (FBR).

## **Advantages of Fast Breeders Reactors**

- FBR’s are designed with several **safety measures**and features which follow**redundancy and** **diversity principle.** Fast Breeder Reactors are safe and efficient apart from the benefits from environmental consideration.
- **Economic viability** of FBR depends on successful operation of Prototype FBR and subsequently successful commissioning and operation of FBR in the country.
- Fast breeder reactors (FBR’s) would use plutonium-239, recovered by reprocessing spent fuel from the first stage, and natural uranium.
- Electricity generated FBR would be a source of **green energy** as the waste from the first nuclear programme is processed and used as fuel in FBR.
- The spent fuel from this reactor can be fed back into the reactor core several times, till the spent fuel contains only short-lived fission products.
- Breeder reactors use a small core, which is important to sustain chain reaction. Besides, they do not even need a moderator for slowing down neutrons, as they use fast neutrons.
- Further there is no need for a large quantity of fuel material for the annual external feed and thus eliminatestheneedforlargecapacitywastestorage spaces with complex construction features. Since independence India has achieved milestones in nuclear science and related technology. However, India’s true potential can come out once it gets a seat at Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG). The responsible and peaceful use of nuclear resources for development of the country is essential especially in the era of climate change.

## Question 174 (Year: 2016 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

**Question ID: 2016-gs3-q174-unacademy**
**Q12.DiscussIndia’sachievementsinthefieldofSpace Science and Technology. How the application of this technology has helped India in its socio- economic development? (200 Words 12.5 Marks) Tag: Awareness in the field of IT, Computer, Space.**

## Answer

- Discuss application of space technology for India’s socio- economic development.
- **Try to conclude**your answer as per context.**Answer:** India has become a global player in space science and technologies (S&T) development. Space program in India developed under leadership of Dr. Vikram Sarabhai.In1962,IndianNationalCommitteeforSpace Research (INCOSPAR) was established as a precursor to ISRO. Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, having identified the role and importance of space technology in a Nation’s development, provided ISRO the necessary direction to function as an agent of development. In 1972 Government of India constituted space commission and Department of Space was established. Both the institutions regulate and gives directions to India’s space programme.

## **India’s achievents in the field of Space S&T**

## **Launch Vehicles**

- **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV):** After its first successful launch in October 1994, PSLV emerged as the reliable and versatile workhorse launch vehicle of India with 39 consecutively successful missions by June 2017. During 19942017, the vehicle has launched 48 Indian satellites and 209 satellites for customers from abroad. Besides, the vehicle successfully launched two spacecraft – Chandrayaan-1 in 2008 and Mars Orbiter Spacecraft in 2013 – that later travelled to Moon and Mars respectively.
- **Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV** **Mk-II):** ISRO has demonstrated the reliability of indigenous cryogenic technology with the four consecutive successful flights of Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) with indigenous Cryogenic engine & stage.
- **GSLV-Mark III:** The first experimental flight of GSLV MKIII (LVM3-X) wassuccessfully launched onDecember18,2014.Thevaluabledatagenerated from the experimental mission was utilized to improve the robustness of the vehicle. GSAT-19 is the heaviest satellite launched with Indian launch vehicle.
- **Technology demonstration:**The Crew module Atmospheric Re-entry Experiment (CARE) was carried out in the experimental mission of GSLV MkIII on 18th Dec 2014, where the re-entry characteristics and the recovery of the Crew Module was demonstrated.**Satellites- Communication, Navigation and Earth**

## **Observation**

- **Communication Satellites:** Eight communication satellites were successfully launched during the period. Four satellites namely, South Asia Satellite (GSAT-9), GSAT-6, GSAT19 & GSAT-6A, were launched using ISRO’s launch vehicle and balance four satellites (GSAT-15, GSAT-16, GSAT-17 and GSAT-18) were launched using procured launches. South Asia Satellite was launched with theobjectiveofprovidingcommunicationservices over South Asian countries.
- **Satellite Navigation Constellation:** IRNSS is an independent regional navigation satellite system being developed by India. It is designed to provide accurate position information service to users in India as well as the region extending up to 1500 km from its boundary, which is its primary service area. The constellation is named as ‘NavIC’ and dedicated to the nation.
- **Earth Observation Satellites:** The above period also witnessed the launch of seven Earth Observationsatellitesviz.Highresolutionimaging satellites (Cartosat-2 Series), Advanced weather monitoring satellites (INSAT-3DR), Satellite for cyclone tracking, climate, and environmental studies.

## **Space Science Missions**

- **ASTROSAT:** India’s first multi wavelength observatory capable of simultaneously viewing the Universe in the visible, Ultra-Violet and X-ray regions of the electromagnetic spectrum.
- **Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM):** India’s first successful interplanetary mission to planet Mars with an orbiter designed to orbit Mars in an elliptical orbit. The Mission was primarily technological mission for design, planning, management and operations of an interplanetary mission. It was also configured to carry out observation of physical features of mars and carry out limited study of Martian atmosphere.

## **Space Applications**

- **SATCOM & SATNAV Applications:** Doordarshan is presently operating 34 satellite channels and has avastnetworkof67Studiosand1,409Transmitters installed throughout the country.
- **Telecommunication:** Presently, 1404 Satellite Earth Stations of different size are operating in the satellite network of BSNL, Government users, closed user group, commercial users and broadcasters. They are being utilised for telecommunications / broadcasting applications.
- **Telemedicine:** Presently about 130 Telemedicine nodes are operational across the country. An MOU is entered into with Ministry of Health and Family Welfare for operations and establishment of telemedicine nodes, in 2016.

## **Earth observation & Geo Spatial applications**

- **Horticulture Inventory:** Area assessment of major horticultural crops across 185 districts spread over 12 States.
- **Sericulture Development project:** To identify Potential areas for expansion in NE region.

## Question 176 (Year: 2015 | Paper: GS III | Marks: 10)

(250 Words 15 Marks) Tag: Science and technology-developments and their application and effects in everyday life. Awareness in the field of IT, Computer, Space, Robotics, Nanotechnology, and issues relating to intellectual property rights.**

#

## Answer

## **Decoding the Question**

- **In introduction, try to write about the GPS** **Era.**-**In Body,**-**Write about “Standard Positioning** **System (SPS) and Precision positioning** **system(PPS )” in brief.**-**Discuss advantages from IRNSS.**-**In conclusion, try to write about the** **importance of IRNSS.** **Answer:**With the beginning of the space age the foundation of the space guided navigation system was laid. The**GPS(Global Positioning System) Era** is the time in modern technology development when capability to use navigation is widespread and in the hands of common people. This Era is dominated by GPS is a multi-use, spacebased radio navigation system owned by the US Government. First, Navigation System with Timing and Ranging (NAVSTAR) satellite for GPS was launched 1978. The 24 satellite system became fully operational in 1993. At present, two GPS services are

## **provided. They are**

- **The Precise Positioning Service (PPS)** is available primarily to the military of the United States and its allies for users properly equipped with PPS receivers.
- **The Standard Positioning Service (SPS),** as initially described in the SPS Signal Specification, was originally designed to provide civil users with a less accurate positioning capability than PPS. Other countries have fielded their own navigation

## **systems. Systems currently in place or planned are**

- Russia: Global Navigation Satellite System (GLONASS)
- China: BeiDou Satellite Navigation System (BDS)
- regional; Compass (2020, global)
- European Union: Galileo
- India: Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS)
- Japan: Quasi-Zenith Satellite System (QZSS) **Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS):** IRNSS was developed by Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). It consists of seven active satellites. It is designed to provide accurate position information service to users in India as well as the region extending up to 1500 km from its boundary, which is its primary service area. IRNSS will provide

## **two types of services**

- **Standard Positioning Service (SPS)** which is provided to all the users.
- **Restricted Service (RS),** which is an encrypted service provided only to the authorised users.

## **Advantages of IRNSS**

- **Own terrestrial, Aerial and Marine Navigation:** Till now India is dependent on GPS, the USA navigation technology, which is critical for national security. As USA’s GPS provides critical information in military areas, if war happens with Pakistan,USAwilldenyinformationtoIndiaeven, they can provide information to Pakistan.
- Once our own navigation system gets ready India’s dependence over GPS will reduce and help in securing national interest and also add in space diplomacy of India.
- **DisasterManagement:Biggestadvantageofhaving** our own navigation system will help in providing real time information during disasters. This navigation system will also help in coordination among various agencies for disaster management.
- **Vehicle tracking and fleet management:** NavIC or IRNSS will be a game changer in self-controlled vehicles, and this can be very useful once 5G services are launched. Tracking ships, vehicles, trucks on road for making supply chain even faster and responsive.
- **Integration with mobile phones:** Using your own navigation system will help in keeping personal data of any individual within the country. This is very significant when it comes to VVIP and important persons from a national security point of view. Nowadays mobile phones are integrated with GPS but once they are equipped with Indian navigation system, they bring in -number benefits to common citizens.
- **Precise Timing:** Precise timing of any location depends on an accurate navigation system. India thereisdemandforasecondIndianStandardTime for north east India. Accurate timings provided by the navigation system will help in use of time for national productivity and economic growth in an efficient manner.
- **Mapping and Geodetic data capture:** For geographical mapping and collecting various data will become easier for India and scientists. A navigation system will reduce dependence on critical data and mapping on other countries will help in generating relevant data and storing the same within the country.
- **Terrestrialnavigationaidforhikersandtravellers:** Accurate positioning and real time information will help trekking, and various adventure sports activities to take place. Travellers traveling to various other parts of the county now can get better location and information.
- **Visual and voice navigation for drivers:** Accurate positioning and navigation visuals will improve travelling experience for the people and especially drivers. Voice navigation is very significant because of it someone can change their directions without entering coordinates manually. Thus, with just the use of 7 satellites India can opt for better, accurate, trustworthy, and most importantly making India self-reliant in advanced navigation technologies etc. become reality. Having our own navigation system will showcase our technological know-how and also making these technologies availableforeverycitizeniscrucialforthedevelopment of the country.
